made_by: MV2, Munim, Inc. (mv2@munimtech.com). Compiled with AI agents working in MV2's name; not yet checked by a human expert. Text and data CC BY 4.0, code Apache-2.0.
what: One row per headline animal-communication claim that MV2's open projects re-tested with a pre-registered, calibrated test. For each claim: the published-style procedure (or our closest reconstruction of it), how often it reported an effect in simulated or permuted worlds built from the real data with the effect removed, the calibrated test, and the registered verdict on the effect. Rows of kind 'negative' are published claims that an effect is absent; for them the ledger gives the calibrated test and its measured power instead of a false-alarm rate. Every number is copied from the named file in the named repository; nothing here is re-computed.
selection_warning: These claims were chosen because we suspected their test ignored some structure of the data (bouts, days, callers, groups, sessions, rhythm mixtures, unequal button use, file layout, females as units, few clans, finite-memory syntax) or, for negative claims, because no significance test or power analysis was reported. The rates below are therefore not an estimate for the animal-communication literature as a whole, and each world embodies one specific suspected confound.

claims.claim: Eastern and Western chimpanzees drum with different rhythms; Eastern drumming alternates short and long gaps

procedures.procedure: Welch t-test of East against West lag-one autocorrelation with bouts as units (published test, reproduced: t -5.732, df 337.27)
procedures.world: C0: no subspecies difference beyond each bout's own gaps in random order

claims.calibrated: Within-bout permutation: Eastern alternation beyond each bout's own arrangement, p_low 0.0001 (size 0.025). Subspecies difference with communities as units: p_two 0.103 over 11 communities, power 0.275 at the registered effect size.
claims.verdict_note: Alternation in Eastern bouts is real; the subspecies difference is not established once communities are the units (underpowered).

claims.claim: Orangutan long calls have nested isochronous rhythm at two levels

procedures.procedure: Paper-style declaration of nested isochrony: on-band excess of rhythm ratios over a uniform null at p < 0.001, for full pulses and at least one sub-pulse type
procedures.world: Null A: inter-onset intervals shuffled within each train (no sequential structure)

claims.calibrated: Renewal null (within-train shuffle): full pulses on-band share 0.9482 against 0.7871, p 0.0005; local-shuffle null B p 0.0010. Headline BEYOND_RENEWAL_BOTH_LEVELS.
claims.verdict_note: Rhythm is real beyond shuffled calls, though about 57% of the full-pulse excess over uniform is reached by shuffled calls alone.

claims.claim: Sperm whale coda 'vowels' differ in length (a-codas longer than i-codas)
claims.paper: Begus et al. 2025-2026 (sperm whale coda vowels)

procedures.procedure: Published-style a minus i duration contrast within whale, codas as units
procedures.world: Bout-clustered worlds: one vowel per bout, 5% flipped, real durations (no vowel effect within bouts)
procedures.source_key: Calibration: published-style test says 'a longer' in 0.355

claims.calibrated: Within-bout contrast D = +0.1136 s over 20 bouts, rotation p_high 0.0001, but the rotation test itself fired in 0.190 of effect-free worlds (limit 0.10).
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict CALIBRATION_FAILED_WITHIN_BOUTS: the within-bout difference is large but no calibrated test of it exists yet.

claims.claim: Sperm whale coda vowels show coarticulation: the first click of a coda changes when the vowel changes
claims.paper: Begus et al. 2025-2026 (sperm whale coda vowels)

procedures.procedure: Published-style first-click mismatch test, change against no-change pairs
procedures.world: W0: no coarticulation (change labels unrelated to click mismatch)

claims.calibrated: Permutation within tag deployments: first-click excess 0.1578 (p_high 0.0035) but the last click of the previous coda mismatches too (0.1040, p_high 0.0433); the registered asymmetry test fired in 0.205 of W0 worlds. Amendment 1, an exact sign-flip test of symmetry (size 0.053 in 1,000 W0 worlds): A 0.0538, p_high 0.2747; 9 first-only against 7 last-only discordant change pairs; power 0.457 at the full observed first-click effect.
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict CALIBRATION_FAILED for the original asymmetry test; amendment 1 graded UNDERPOWERED: the public pairs cannot tell carryover from a symmetric mismatch at vowel changes.

claims.claim: Egyptian fruit bat calls carry information about the addressee
claims.paper: Prat, Taub and Yovel 2016, Scientific Reports 6:39419

procedures.procedure: Addressee classifier with labels shuffled freely across the data set (published-style)
procedures.world: Labels follow which bats were addressed on which recording days only

claims.calibrated: Shuffles within each emitter's recording day: mean balanced accuracy 0.526 against a day-blocked null of 0.447, p 0.005; 0 of 4 day-only worlds detected, 5 of 5 planted-effect worlds detected.
claims.verdict_note: About 44% of the published-style excess is reachable by day composition alone, but the rest survives.

claims.claim: African elephants address one another with individually specific name-like calls
claims.paper: Pardo et al. 2024, Nature Ecology and Evolution

procedures.procedure: Receiver labels shuffled within caller and relationship across dates (naive null)
procedures.world: Drift worlds: call features drift with time, no receiver-specific calls

claims.calibrated: Shuffles within caller, date and relationship: p 0.383, but only 4 informative blocks (11 calls) and power 0.05.
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict UNDERPOWERED: the public data cannot separate names from day effects.

claims.claim: Wild chimpanzee 'additive' call pairs combine two meanings to report two concurrent events

procedures.procedure: Published criterion: A and B are the two single calls closest to the pair's average event profile
procedures.world: Pure A-or-B mixtures built from real utterances (nothing added)

claims.calibrated: Per-utterance conjunction test: the A-or-B mixture was rejected for 0 of 8 additive pairs; for the 3 pairs with at least 80% power the label is mixture not rejected.
claims.verdict_note: Where the test had power, the pairs behave like a mixture of the two calls' situations; five pairs are underpowered.

claims.claim: Sooty mangabeys change the meaning of a call pair by its order
claims.paper: Le Floch et al. 2026, BMC Biology

procedures.procedure: Caller-blind pooled test of order against context (our stand-in; the paper used a Bayesian model)
procedures.world: W0: order labels permuted within caller

claims.calibrated: Exact conditional test within 15 females: T 20 against null mean 7.061, p two-sided 0.0002; every leave-one-female-out p at most 0.0075; false-alarm rate 0.021.
claims.verdict_note: Flag DAY_CONFOUND: the female-by-day test has too few same-day pairs to be informative.

claims.claim: Sperm whale codas combine a rhythm with one of five discrete tempo types

procedures.procedure: Five tempo peaks in the pooled histogram of coda durations (published evidence for tempo types)
procedures.world: Each rhythm's durations drawn from a single-peaked distribution (tempo-free)

procedures.procedure: Number of occupied rhythm-tempo combinations (34 in the real codas)
procedures.world: Same tempo-free surrogates cut at the same four tempo boundaries

claims.calibrated: 0 of 999 tempo-free surrogates show all five pooled peaks; the clan's commonest coda 1+1+3 is multimodal (Silverman p 0.001, Holm) and multimodal inside 4 of 10 social units; test size at most 0.02.
claims.verdict_note: Tempo types are real; the combination count, by contrast, is reached by every tempo-free surrogate and is no evidence of free combination.

claims.claim: Spotted hyena whoops carry individual but not group (clan) signatures
claims.paper: Lehmann et al. 2022, Proceedings of the Royal Society B 289:20220548

power.planted: Clan offset drawn from 0.5^2 times the covariance of the hyenas' mean whoops (clans differ half as much as individuals), in relabeled worlds

claims.calibrated: Leave-one-hyena-out clan accuracy 0.2403 against a whole-hyena relabeling null of mean 0.2207, p 0.34 (299 worlds); handheld only p 0.1767; females only p 0.575. Authors' scheme reproduced (0.3458 against chance 0.2573); its excess is not significant, p 0.09 (99 worlds).
claims.verdict_note: The negative holds: no clan signal under a calibrated test that found a planted clan offset a quarter the size of individual differences in 40 of 40 worlds. Power covers whole-whoop shifts only.

claims.claim: Western Australian magpie call sequences have second-order structure: each call depends on the two calls before it
claims.paper: Mason, Walsh, King and Ridley 2026, bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.06.15.732496 (preprint)

procedures.procedure: Order-2 against order-1 Markov chain chosen by AIC on the pooled sequence types, observed transitions counted as parameters (our type-level stand-in)
procedures.world: H0b: each social group's own first-order chain, with looped chunks kept as loops (no second-order rule)

procedures.procedure: Preprint's own model comparison, rebuilt from its Methods: order-2 against order-1 in-sample log-likelihood with additive smoothing k 0.0001 to 1, averaged over k, no penalty and no held-out data (type level)
procedures.world: H0p: every sequence type redrawn at its own length from one pooled first-order chain (no second-order rule, no groups, no loops)

procedures.procedure: Preprint's own significance test, rebuilt from its Methods: each second-order transition probability against 10,000 zero-order token permutations, Benjamini-Hochberg at 0.05; fires if any cell is significant (type level)
procedures.world: H0p: pooled first-order worlds as above (first 200 worlds)

claims.calibrated: Leave-one-type-out, group-aware gain of order 2 over order 1: G 0.0000 nats on 224 group records (lambda chosen 0), p 1.0 against group first-order worlds with and without loops (999 each); power 0.935 at rho 0.3. The preprint's own procedures both fire on the real types (in-sample gain 78.29 nats; 3 significant cells), but the real in-sample gain is below the 5th percentile of every first-order null (78.67 pooled, 87.99 group, 91.30 group with loops) and 3 cells is typical of them (share of group-with-loops worlds with at least 3: 0.886). Type-level data only.
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict POOLING_EXPLAINS at the level of sequence types: within groups the call two back adds nothing. Amendment 1 rebuilt the preprint's own two procedures and graded both UNSAFE: the in-sample comparison fired in 2,997 of 2,997 first-order worlds and the zero-order permutation test in 0.49 of pooled and 0.94 of group-with-loops first-order worlds. The token-level claim is untested because those data are not public.

claims.claim: Soundboard-trained dogs' two-button combinations form non-random networks: each dog's Randomness Index lies well below that of Erdos-Renyi random graphs
claims.paper: Bastos, Houghton, Naranjo and Rossano 2024, Scientific Reports 14:28771

procedures.procedure: Authors' per-dog criterion: Randomness Index at least 0.2 below the mean of Erdos-Renyi graphs of the same size and density (concept-level networks of pairs seen at least twice)
procedures.world: Each eligible dog's own pair events re-paired at random so that every concept keeps its number of pairings (button popularity only, no pairing preference); criterion applied to the mean of 1,000 re-pairings per dog, one world per dog
procedures.source_key: eligible rows with ri_pop_mean < ri_er_mean - 0.2 (checked by test_reading_counts.py)

claims.calibrated: Popularity-only null over 133 dogs: mean real RI -0.564 against -0.766 for popularity and -0.209 for Erdos-Renyi; popularity explains 1.566 of the Erdos-Renyi gap; group p (real more negative than popularity) 1.0; 24 of 133 dogs pass the authors' criterion against popularity (93 against Erdos-Renyi); 7 have per-dog p <= 0.05.
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict POPULARITY_EXPLAINS_MOST_OF_GAP: unequal button use alone gives a more negative index than the dogs' own networks. Only the network evidence is tested; the paper's population-level pair model with a popularity offset and its non-imitation result are untouched. Public concept-level tables, not the paper's button-label networks.

claims.claim: Wild yellow-naped amazon pairs follow more than 20 syntactic rules in their warble duets (call types assort non-randomly)
claims.paper: Dahlin, Killinger, Snipe, Small, Guenther and Richwine 2026, Journal of Avian Biology e03552

procedures.procedure: Pooled permutation test of adjacent call-type dependence across all duets (the naive 'calls assort non-randomly' test; our stand-in, since the paper's Voyant correlations have no null model)
procedures.world: W0: each call's type redrawn from its own pair's calls of the same sex (no order and no co-occurrence beyond each pair's repertoire)

claims.calibrated: Adjacent order beyond each duet's own calls (shuffles within duet and sex): 2.2416 bits against 1.8916, p 0.0001, test size 0.030; co-occurrence within 5 calls beyond each pair's repertoire: p 0.0001, size 0.045; 9 ordered call pairs survive Benjamini-Hochberg under the within-duet null. The paper's Table 1 is reproduced (14 of 15 between-type rows to three decimals) as correlations of call-type counts across 10 equal slices of the data file; 16.7% of those pairs stay significant when whole duets are placed in random order.
claims.verdict_note: Registered headline SYNTAX_BEYOND_REPERTOIRE: the duets are ordered, but the published 'rules' measure where duets sit in the file, not call order. Power to one planted weak rule was only 0.105; robustness checks (leave one pair out, repeated duets, position-only null) are queued as AMENDMENT-2.

claims.claim: Common marmoset call sequences are best described by a second-order Markov model: each call depends on the two calls before it
claims.paper: Bosshard, Burkart, Merlo, Cathcart, Townsend and Bickel 2024, Royal Society Open Science 11:240218

procedures.procedure: Authors' reading of their leave-one-sequence-out cross-validation: order 2 beats order 1 at every smoothing constant (alpha 0.0001 to 1), reproduced on their public file
procedures.world: H0p: every sequence redrawn at its own length from one pooled first-order chain (no second-order rule)

claims.calibrated: Real D_best (best order 2 minus best order 1, held-out log-likelihood) 303.20 nats over 5,801 sequences in 120 sessions; 297.35 when whole sessions are held out. Against session-specific first-order worlds the largest D_best was 22.62 (p 0.0020) and with looped chunks 52.40 (p 0.0020, 499 worlds each); the authors' reading fired in 0 of 499 worlds of each of the four nulls; power 1.0 at rho 0.3.
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict SECOND_ORDER_SURVIVES: not explained by pooling sessions or looping chunks, and the authors' test is well calibrated against both. A position-only explanation (the start padding tells order 2 it is predicting the second call) is not yet excluded; it is registered as AMENDMENT-1-POSITION.md.

claims.claim: Reproductively available female bottlenose dolphins avoid the signature whistles of more coercive (frequently consorting) males more strongly
claims.paper: Bouchard, Allen, Sorensen, Kruetzen, Marfurt, Connor and King 2026, PNAS 123(24):e2531602123

procedures.procedure: Trial-level OLS interaction of avoidance distance on consort score by reproductive state, 34 playbacks treated as independent, two-sided p <= 0.05 (our stand-in for the paper's mixed model)
procedures.world: Reproductive-state label given to 7 of the 17 females at random, each female's playbacks kept together (all 19,448 labelings, exact)

claims.calibrated: Exact female-level test over all 19,448 labelings: slope difference 557.65 m per unit of consort score, one-sided p 0.0053; largest leave-one-female-out p 0.0195 (HRS), leave-one-male-out 0.0854 (RID), leave-one-playback-out 0.0324. Rank version p 0.0855; consort scores shuffled among males p 0.0502. Secondary effects at the female level: association by state p 0.878, response duration p 0.140 (two-sided).
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict SURVIVES_AT_FEMALE_LEVEL: the headline holds with females as the units. It rests on the size of a few long avoidances (rank version p 0.0855), and the two secondary effects are not significant at the female level.

claims.claim: Western Australian magpie fledglings produce the call sequences of their own social group rather than those of the wider population (socially learned sequences)
claims.paper: Mason, King and Ridley 2026, Proceedings of the Royal Society B 293:20251620

procedures.procedure: Authors' decision, reproduced: binomial mixed model of fledgling presence of a sequence type on its presence in the group record (no term for the type), group coefficient positive with Wald p <= 0.05 and lowest AICc of three models
procedures.world: Donor worlds: each fledgling given the real group and extra-group records of a fledgling from a different group (a group it never lived in)

claims.calibrated: Own-group overlap excess against 9,999 random group assignments keeping group sizes: D 0.1467, p 0.0124 (secondary file D 0.1756, p 0.0042); this test fired in 1 of 200 donor worlds and found a planted effect in 50 of 50. Group-specific order beyond content: D_ord 0.0347, p 0.1612, power 0.14. Contacts against repertoire size with effort removed: rho -0.879.
claims.verdict_note: Registered reading OWN_GROUP_EXCESS: fledglings do match their own group. But the published decision reported 'group repertoire predicts' in 200 of 200 worlds with a foreign group's records, so the published evidence does not measure it; group-specific call order is untested with power (0.14).

claims.claim: Pacific sperm whale clans' identity codas become less alike the more two clans share ocean, while their other codas do not (symbolic marking of clan identity)

procedures.procedure: Published identity Mantel test of between-clan identity-coda similarity on spatial overlap, one-tailed p <= 0.05 (authors' Figure 4 values, reproduced: r -0.4986, exact p 0.0409)
procedures.world: Every relabeling of the 7 clans in the overlap matrix (no link between overlap and coda similarity; all 5,040, exact)

procedures.procedure: Published declaration: identity Mantel p <= 0.05 and non-identity Mantel p > 0.05
procedures.world: Every relabeling of the 7 clans, as above (all 5,040, exact)

claims.calibrated: Exact test of the identity minus non-identity difference over all 5,040 relabelings: D -0.4223, p 0.0911; leaving one clan out, the identity trend keeps p <= 0.05 in 2 of 7 sets. With the authors' similarity, the trend survives a sampling-effort control (partial r -0.5742, p 0.0165) and holds at p <= 0.05 in 5 of 9 overlap definitions. A within-clan test (identity-coda share higher where clans meet, 0.117, p 0.0401) was circular: with identity types re-derived without the scored region, 0.0559, p 0.1099, and a typicality placebo fires the same test (p 0.0356).
claims.verdict_note: Registered verdict ID_TREND_WITHOUT_CONTRAST; post hoc amendment 1 EMPHASIS_LOST_UNDER_LOCO. The published test is exactly sized and the trend is robust to sampling effort, but 7 clans cannot show that the effect is specific to identity codas, and the one within-clan test that seemed to support marking was circular.

claims.claim: Bengalese finch song has structure beyond Markov dynamics, consistent with hierarchy, because the mutual information between syllables decays as an exponential plus a power law
claims.paper: Sainburg, Theilman, Thielk and Gentner 2019, Nature Communications 10:3636

procedures.procedure: Published verdict, reproduced with the paper's design (bouts joined, bird-days pooled): the composite exponential-plus-power-law model has the lowest AICc with relative weight above 0.999
procedures.world: Each bird's own k-th order Markov syntax (k 2 to 8, chosen by held-out likelihood) fitted to the real song; bouts drawn independently, real number of bouts per day (no structure beyond an 8-syllable memory)

procedures.procedure: Same published verdict, in the registered self-check
procedures.world: S1: simulated per-bird phrase machines (fixed phrases sung in runs, sparse first-order phrase transitions; finite-state)

claims.calibrated: Real exponential-minus-composite AICc gap 138.84 on 215,740 syllables (4 birds, 18 bird-days, figshare 4805749 v9); per-bird k-gram surrogates: 100 of 100 fire, 95th percentile 156.17, p_upper 0.4752; bouts reordered within days: 100 of 100 fire, p 0.1485. The registered test is calibrated (0 of 12 in-class and 1 of 12 phrase-machine worlds flagged) and flagged 12 of 12 worlds with planted within-bout recursion, which the composite verdict itself caught in 1 of 12.
claims.verdict_note: Registered grade FINITE_STATE_SUFFICES: on Bengalese finch song the composite verdict is fully reproduced by each bird's finite-memory syntax with independent bouts, so it is no evidence of hierarchy in this species. Hierarchy is not ruled out; one of the paper's four species; house finch, Cassin's vireo, chimpanzee and speech stages are queued.

graded_without_false_alarm_rate.claim: Naked mole-rat soft chirps carry a colony-specific dialect
graded_without_false_alarm_rate.paper: Barker, Veviurko, Bennett, Hart, Mograby and Lewin 2021, Science 371:503
graded_without_false_alarm_rate.calibrated: Leave one recording date out with no test rat in training: balanced-accuracy excess 0.1048 (2 colonies, 4,043 chirps), p 0.0100 against a day-only Gaussian world (mean -0.0698), power 0.80. Published-style rat-grouped score 0.4004 against a day-only mean of 0.0952, p 0.0050. Authors' Random Forest reproduced (accuracy 0.6647, chance 0.25) but its leave-one-date-out excess is -0.0725.
graded_without_false_alarm_rate.verdict_note: Registered verdict COLONY_SIGNATURE_TRANSFERS_ACROSS_DAYS, weakly and for 2 colonies. No false-alarm rate of the published procedure was registered, so the row is not in the claims table.
